From 58189ca7b27411c3dc9a5cb9eeee0906da684c59 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: David Ahern <dsa@cumulusnetworks.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2015 15:10:50 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] net: Fix vti use case with oif in dst lookups

Steffen reported that the recent change to add oif to dst lookups breaks
the VTI use case. The problem is that with the oif set in the flow struct
the comparison to the nh_oif is triggered. Fix by splitting the
FLOWI_FLAG_VRFSRC into 2 flags -- one that triggers the vrf device cache
bypass (FLOWI_FLAG_VRFSRC) and another telling the lookup to not compare
nh oif (FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF).

Fixes: 42a7b32b73d6 ("xfrm: Add oif to dst lookups")

Signed-off-by: David Ahern <dsa@cumulusnetworks.com>
Acked-by: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/include/net/flow.h b/include/net/flow.h
index acd6a096250e..9b85db85f13c 100644
--- a/include/net/flow.h
+++ b/include/net/flow.h
@@ -35,6 +35,7 @@ struct flowi_common {
 #define FLOWI_FLAG_ANYSRC		0x01
 #define FLOWI_FLAG_KNOWN_NH		0x02
 #define FLOWI_FLAG_VRFSRC		0x04
+#define FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF		0x08
 	__u32	flowic_secid;
 	struct flowi_tunnel flowic_tun_key;
 };

diff --git a/include/net/route.h b/include/net/route.h
index cc61cb95f059..f46af256880c 100644
--- a/include/net/route.h
+++ b/include/net/route.h
@@ -255,7 +255,7 @@ static inline void ip_route_connect_init(struct flowi4 *fl4, __be32 dst, __be32
 		flow_flags |= FLOWI_FLAG_ANYSRC;
 
 	if (netif_index_is_vrf(sock_net(sk), oif))
-		flow_flags |= FLOWI_FLAG_VRFSRC;
+		flow_flags |= FLOWI_FLAG_VRFSRC | FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF;
 
 	flowi4_init_output(fl4, oif, sk->sk_mark, tos, RT_SCOPE_UNIVERSE,
 			   protocol, flow_flags, dst, src, dport, sport);

diff --git a/drivers/net/vrf.c b/drivers/net/vrf.c
index e7094fbd7568..488c6f50df73 100644
--- a/drivers/net/vrf.c
+++ b/drivers/net/vrf.c
@@ -193,7 +193,8 @@ static netdev_tx_t vrf_process_v4_outbound(struct sk_buff *skb,
 		.flowi4_oif = vrf_dev->ifindex,
 		.flowi4_iif = LOOPBACK_IFINDEX,
 		.flowi4_tos = RT_TOS(ip4h->tos),
-		.flowi4_flags = FLOWI_FLAG_ANYSRC | FLOWI_FLAG_VRFSRC,
+		.flowi4_flags = FLOWI_FLAG_ANYSRC | FLOWI_FLAG_VRFSRC |
+				FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF,
 		.daddr = ip4h->daddr,
 	};
 

diff --git a/net/ipv4/fib_trie.c b/net/ipv4/fib_trie.c
index 26d6ffb6d23c..6c2af797f2f9 100644
--- a/net/ipv4/fib_trie.c
+++ b/net/ipv4/fib_trie.c
@@ -1426,7 +1426,7 @@ int fib_table_lookup(struct fib_table *tb, const struct flowi4 *flp,
 			    nh->nh_flags & RTNH_F_LINKDOWN &&
 			    !(fib_flags & FIB_LOOKUP_IGNORE_LINKSTATE))
 				continue;
-			if (!(flp->flowi4_flags & FLOWI_FLAG_VRFSRC)) {
+			if (!(flp->flowi4_flags & FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF)) {
 				if (flp->flowi4_oif &&
 				    flp->flowi4_oif != nh->nh_oif)
 					continue;

diff --git a/net/ipv4/xfrm4_policy.c b/net/ipv4/xfrm4_policy.c
index bb919b28619f..c10a9ee68433 100644
--- a/net/ipv4/xfrm4_policy.c
+++ b/net/ipv4/xfrm4_policy.c
@@ -33,6 +33,8 @@ static struct dst_entry *__xfrm4_dst_lookup(struct net *net, struct flowi4 *fl4,
 	if (saddr)
 		fl4->saddr = saddr->a4;
 
+	fl4->flowi4_flags = FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF;
+
 	rt = __ip_route_output_key(net, fl4);
 	if (!IS_ERR(rt))
 		return &rt->dst;
-- 
2.25.1



diff --git a/net/ipv4/udp.c b/net/ipv4/udp.c
index c0a15e7f359f..f7d1d5e19e95 100644
--- a/net/ipv4/udp.c
+++ b/net/ipv4/udp.c
@@ -1024,7 +1024,8 @@ int udp_sendmsg(struct sock *sk, struct msghdr *msg, size_t len)
 		if (netif_index_is_vrf(net, ipc.oif)) {
 			flowi4_init_output(fl4, ipc.oif, sk->sk_mark, tos,
 					   RT_SCOPE_UNIVERSE, sk->sk_protocol,
-					   (flow_flags | FLOWI_FLAG_VRFSRC),
+					   (flow_flags | FLOWI_FLAG_VRFSRC |
+					    FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF),
 					   faddr, saddr, dport,
 					   inet->inet_sport);

### Modifications in Each File

1. **`include/net/flow.h`**
   - Added a new flag `FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF` (value `0x08`) to the `flowi_common` structure.

2. **`include/net/route.h`**
   - Modified the logic in `ip_route_connect_init` to include the new flag `FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF` when the `oif` is a VRF index. This change ensures that the lookup does not compare the next-hop output interface (nh_oif).

3. **`drivers/net/vrf.c`**
   - Updated the `vrf_process_v4_outbound` function to include the `FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF` flag in the `flowi4_flags` when processing outbound packets.

4. **`net/ipv4/fib_trie.c`**
   - Changed the condition in `fib_table_lookup` to check for `FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF` instead of `FLOWI_FLAG_VRFSRC`. This adjustment allows the lookup to bypass the nh_oif comparison when the new flag is set.

5. **`net/ipv4/xfrm4_policy.c`**
   - Set the `flowi4_flags` to include `FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF` in the `__xfrm4_dst_lookup` function, ensuring that this flag is used during destination lookups.

6. **`net/ipv4/udp.c`**
   - Modified the `udp_sendmsg` function to include `FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF` in the flow flags when the `oif` is a VRF index, similar to the changes made in `ip_route_connect_init`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications across the files are interconnected as they collectively address the issue reported regarding the VTI use case and the recent changes that introduced the `oif` in destination lookups. The introduction of the `FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF` flag allows for more granular control over the flow lookup process, specifically enabling the bypass of the next-hop output interface comparison when necessary.

- The new flag is defined in `flow.h` and is utilized in various functions across the routing and networking layers (`route.h`, `vrf.c`, `fib_trie.c`, `xfrm4_policy.c`, and `udp.c`).
- The changes in `route.h` and `vrf.c` ensure that the flag is set correctly when dealing with VRF indices, while the adjustments in `fib_trie.c` and `xfrm4_policy.c` ensure that the lookup logic respects this new flag.
- The modifications in `udp.c` ensure that the UDP protocol handling also adheres to the new logic introduced by the flag, maintaining consistency across the networking stack. 

Overall, these changes work together to fix the bug by allowing the system to correctly handle cases where the next-hop output interface should not be compared, thus restoring the intended functionality of the VTI use case.

   - Modified the logic to set the `flow_flags` to include `FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF` when the output interface is a VRF, ensuring that the nh_oif comparison is skipped.

   - Similar to the previous files, the `flow_flags` in the `udp_sendmsg` function is updated to include `FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF`, allowing the UDP packets to bypass the nh_oif comparison.

The modifications across the files are interconnected as they all aim to address the same issue related to the output interface (oif) comparison in destination lookups, particularly in the context of Virtual Routing and Forwarding (VRF) use cases.

- The changes in `fib_trie.c`, `xfrm4_policy.c`, `vrf.c`, `route.h`, and `udp.c` ensure that when this flag is set, the logic correctly avoids the nh_oif comparison, thus fixing the bug reported by Steffen regarding the VTI use case. 

Overall, the patch effectively splits the existing flag functionality to provide more granular control over the flow lookup process, specifically for scenarios involving VRF and VTI.

        Commit message:
        net: Fix vti use case with oif in dst lookups

Steffen reported that the recent change to add oif to dst lookups breaks
the VTI use case. The problem is that with the oif set in the flow struct
the comparison to the nh_oif is triggered. Fix by splitting the
FLOWI_FLAG_VRFSRC into 2 flags -- one that triggers the vrf device cache
bypass (FLOWI_FLAG_VRFSRC) and another telling the lookup to not compare
nh oif (FLOWI_FLAG_SKIP_NH_OIF).
